A recipient with no access to the provisioning node, no second machine, and no technical skill still answers the only question that matters — is this the good that was provisioned? The weakest receiver is handed the same certainty as the provisioner. **Verify-by-receipt is what makes a locally-held good universally checkable -- the good stays in its node, but its proof travels to whoever holds the receipt.** This closes the circle the earlier chapters opened. Because the receipt carries everything and `verify_provision` needs nothing else, a good held locally at one node (Chapter 3) is confirmable by anyone who receives its receipt. The provision was gated by a human (Chapter 4); the receiver sees that in the receipt too. Local holding and universal verifiability coexist precisely because the check is against the receipt, not a registry. The good is sovereign and its proof is portable. **A good verifiable by its own receipt is a good you can hold and verify -- provisioned locally, gated by a human, and confirmable by the weakest receiver, which is what the whole primitive was for.** The result is the promise of the volume, made checkable. A physical good is provisioned as a receipted governed object, held by its node, stood behind by a human, and verifiable by whoever receives it — all without a central registry anyone must trust. A receiver does not take the good on faith; they read its light. Chapter 6 names exactly what this primitive composes and what it homes out. **In the acceptance tests, a good verifies by receipt with no registry, and a tampered good or receipt flips to tampered -- so the verify-by-receipt, weakest-party discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_verify_provision_by_receipt_no_registry`, `test_verify_provision_detects_a_tampered_good`, and `test_verify_provision_detects_a_tampered_receipt` prove the three cases. For Ridgeline, this means anyone the homestead hands a good to — a family member, a neighbor, a buyer — can confirm from the receipt alone that it is the good the homestead sovereignly provisioned, with no call to Ridgeline and no expertise. Chapter 6 draws the map of composed floors and homed-out concerns.

title: S9 01 Material Primitive
chapter_title: What The Material Primitive Composes -- The Object Model, Provenance, Mandate, and the Gate
text: You will see exactly what this primitive builds on and what it deliberately leaves out -- it composes the Object Model, the provenance rule, the mandate scope, and the human gate, and homes economic value, estate, and the material verticals to their own series -- so the boundary of the primitive is drawn as precisely as its center.

title: S9 01 Material Primitive
chapter_title: What The Material Primitive Composes -- The Object Model, Provenance, Mandate, and the Gate
text: **An opener is defined by what it composes -- this primitive stands on the sealed floors of the record series and adds exactly one thing: provisioning matter as a governed object.** The first volume of a new series is not a monolith; it is a composition. This chapter draws the map. `provision_local` builds on the Object Model for the governed object, the provenance rule for honest citation, the mandate scope for one-object-one-scope, and the HumanApprovalGate for human primacy — and it adds one new thing, the material provision itself. Naming the composition is how the opener stays honest about where each guarantee actually lives. **It composes the Object Model (S5 Vol 5) for the governed object -- every provision is a hash-chained, mandate-scoped version, so the good inherits governance it does not re-implement.** The Object Model is the foundation. `provision_local` provisions through `ObjectRegistry.append`, and `verify_provision` re-derives through `make_version`. The hash-chaining, the one-object-one-mandate binding, the version identity — all of it comes from the Object Model. The primitive does not build its own object store; it composes the record series' own and points it at a physical good. **It composes the receipts/provenance rule (P5) -- a good's source citation must resolve, so a provenance is never written false, the same honesty the record layer holds.** The provenance rule travels with the object. Because `provision_local` provisions through the Object Model, a good's `source_ref` must resolve or the provision is refused (P5) — a citation is never written false. A good's stated origin is held to the same standard as a record's. The primitive gets this honesty for free by composing the floor; it does not weaken it for matter. **It composes the mandate scope (S5 Vol 28) -- a good belongs to exactly one mandate, so provisioning respects the same scoping that governs records.** Scope is the record layer's, applied to goods. A provisioned good is bound to exactly one mandate, and the Object Model refuses to move it — proven when a re-provision under a second mandate is rejected. A good cannot straddle two scopes any more than a record can. The mandate that governs who may see and change a record now governs who provisions a good, one consistent scoping across data and matter. **It composes the HumanApprovalGate (S5 Vol 16) -- a gated material provision passes a human, so human primacy over matter is the compliance layer's gate, not a new one.** The human hand is the compliance floor's. `provision_local` composes the HumanApprovalGate the compliance series already enforces for high-materiality actions, so a gated physical provision passes the same oversight a sensitive record change does. Enforcement of human primacy lives where it always did; the primitive points it at matter and reuses it. **It homes the good's economic value OUT to Sovereign Economy (S10) and its material estate to Generational Transfer (S12) -- the primitive provisions the good, it does not price it or inherit it.** The honest boundary in one line. A provisioned good has an economic value — what it is worth, how it trades — and that is not this volume; it homes OUT to Sovereign Economy (Series 10). A provisioned good is also part of an estate that passes to a successor, and that homes to Generational Transfer (Series 12). `provision_local` provisions and verifies the good; it does not price it, trade it, or inherit it. Those are their own capabilities with their own homes. **It homes energy, food and water, shelter, logistics, and the provision covenant to the volumes that follow -- this opener is the primitive under all of them, not the verticals themselves.** The rest of the series is named, not built here. Energy provisioning homes to S9 Vol 2, food and water to Vol 3, shelter to Vol 4, logistics to Vol 5, and the provision covenant that binds them to Vol 6. This volume builds the primitive every one of those stands on — provisioning a good as a receipted governed object — and points each vertical at its own volume. The opener claims the primitive and only the primitive; the material domains are their own volumes. **Drawing the boundary precisely is what makes the opener trustworthy -- it claims exactly the material provision, composes its guarantees from named sealed floors, and points every other concern at its real home.** The value of the map is that nothing floats. The governed object is the Object Model's. Provenance is P5's. Scope is the mandate's. Human primacy is the gate's. Economic value is S10's, estate is S12's, and the verticals are Vols 2–6's. What is left — and all that is left — for this volume is the material provision: provisioning a good as a receipted, locally-held, human-gated, receipt-verifiable governed object. An opener that names its boundary this precisely is one a reader can trust exactly, because every guarantee has a stated, checkable home.

title: S9 01 Material Primitive
chapter_title: The Material Primitive vs the Central Asset Registry
text: You will see the two approaches set side by side -- a good tracked in a central registry a node cannot audit versus one provisioned as a locally-held, receipt-verifiable governed object -- so the sovereign choice between them is explicit, not implied.

title: S9 01 Material Primitive
chapter_title: The Material Primitive vs the Central Asset Registry
text: **The choice is between a good you reference and a good you hold -- a central registry entry versus a locally-held receipted object -- and the difference is whether a node controls the truth about its own matter.** Every node tracks its goods somehow; the question is only whether the truth lives in a system it controls. This chapter sets the two side by side. The central asset registry keeps the truth in a provider's database the node must query and cannot audit. The material primitive keeps the truth in the node's own registry, in a receipt that travels with the good. The contrast is the argument of the whole volume, made explicit. **The central registry keeps the truth in a system the node cannot audit -- the node references a row it does not control, and confirmation means asking the provider.** A central registry is a reference, not a holding. The node's good is represented by a row in a provider's database — an asset management platform, a manufacturer's serial registry — that the node can read but not audit and cannot change on its own terms. To confirm what it has, the node queries the provider. The truth about the node's own matter lives outside the node, in a system whose operator, not the holder, is authoritative. **The material primitive keeps the truth in the node's own registry and the good's own receipt -- the node holds the object and confirms it without asking anyone.** The sovereign answer moves the truth home. `provision_local` records the good in the node's own Object Model registry, and the receipt that travels with the good carries its own proof. The node holds the object and can confirm it — or hand a receiver the means to confirm it — without querying any provider. The truth about the node's matter lives in the node and in the receipt, where the holder is authoritative. **The central registry can change without the node -- a row can be revised, revoked, or lost, and the node has no independent record -- while the primitive's receipt re-derives or fails.** With a central registry, the record is the provider's to alter. A row can be edited, a record revoked, an entry lost in a migration, and the node holding the good has no independent copy to check against. With the primitive, the receipt is hash-chained: it either re-derives from its own fields or it does not, and any alteration shows as tampered. The difference is between a record someone else can quietly change and one that cannot be changed without the change being visible. **The central registry is a single point of failure and control -- its outage or capture breaks every node -- while local provisioning depends on no shared system.** A central registry concentrates risk. Its availability bounds every node's ability to confirm a good; its compromise corrupts every node's records; its operator holds power over all of them. Local provisioning removes that point: each node holds its own goods, and a receiver verifies by receipt, so there is no shared system whose failure or capture breaks the whole. The primitive is resilient exactly where the central registry is fragile — at the single point everything depends on. **The central registry requires access and trust to check a good -- while the primitive's receipt is verifiable by the weakest receiver with no access at all.** A central registry serves those with credentials. To confirm a good, you need a login, a query, and trust that the provider's answer is honest. The primitive lowers that bar to nothing: `verify_provision` checks the receipt in hand, so a receiver with no access to any system and no expertise still confirms the good. Verifiability by anyone who holds the receipt replaces verifiability by those with database access — which, for a good that changes hands, is precisely who needs to check it. **Choosing the material primitive is a sovereign choice -- it is what lets a node control the truth about its own matter, held and verifiable rather than referenced and trusted.** This is the sovereignty frame. A good known only through a provider's registry is a good the node does not fully own — the provider controls its record and its confirmation. A good provisioned as a locally-held, receipt-verifiable object is one the node owns in full: held on its own storage, under its own mandate, stood behind by its own human, and confirmable without anyone's permission. The sovereign asset is not the row in someone's database; it is the good you hold and the receipt you can verify. **The contrast is not convenience versus features -- it is referenced-and-trusted versus held-and-verifiable, which for a node's physical goods is the whole game.** It would be easy to read this as a nicer asset tracker. It is not. The central registry and the material primitive differ on the one axis that matters for sovereignty: whether the node controls the truth about its own matter. A node whose goods can be revised, revoked, or lost by a provider it cannot audit does not sovereignly hold them, however convenient the platform. The material primitive makes goods sovereign by making them held and verifiable. Chapter 8 draws the primitive together and opens the series.

title: S9 01 Material Primitive
chapter_title: A Good You Can Hold and Verify
text: You will see the whole volume drawn together -- a good provisioned as a receipted governed object, held locally with no central provisioner, gated by a human, and verifiable by receipt -- and with it the material layer opened: the sovereign discipline of records extended to matter.

title: S9 01 Material Primitive
chapter_title: A Good You Can Hold and Verify
text: **The Material Primitive makes present one thing -- a good provisioned as a receipted, mandate-scoped governed object a node holds, gates, and can verify by receipt -- and that one thing is the primitive the rest of Material Sovereignty is built on.** Five series made records sovereign; this opener extends the discipline to matter. `provision_local` provisions a physical good as a governed object in the node's own registry; a human gate stands behind the consequential act; `verify_provision` confirms the good from its receipt alone. A physical good becomes as held and verifiable as a record — which is what the whole series reaches toward: not just data you can trust, but matter you can hold and prove. **The good is provisioned as a receipted governed object -- hash-chained, mandate-scoped, provenance-true -- so a physical thing carries the same verifiable receipt as a sovereign record.** The first pillar is the governed object. `provision_local` composes the Object Model to provision a good as a hash-chained version bound to one mandate, with a source that must resolve. The good's receipt travels with it and re-derives or fails. Matter inherits the exact integrity the record layer holds: a good is not a row in a database but a governed object whose receipt anyone can check. **It is held locally with no central provisioner -- each node provisions into its own registry, so no node depends on a provisioner it does not control, and yet a receipt verifies anywhere.** The second pillar is local holding. `provision_local` writes into the node's own registry; two nodes provision independently; and a receipt from one verifies at another by receipt alone. There is no central provisioner whose outage, capture, or revision breaks the whole. Goods are held where they are, and their proofs travel — sovereign and shareable at once. **Human primacy holds over the physical act -- a gated material provision passes a human before it is recorded, and the receipt carries the approver.** The third pillar is the human hand. When a material provision requires approval, `provision_local` refuses it without a human and, with one, records the approver in the receipt. A physical act — harder to reverse than a data change — carries a person's judgment in its permanent record. The consequential provisioning of matter is not left to an unchecked automation; a human stands behind it, verifiably. **The check is weakest-party verifiable -- verify_provision re-derives the receipt from its own fields and confirms the good, so a resourceless receiver reads a green light with no registry, no second device, no expertise.** The fourth pillar is the one that makes a good universally trustworthy. `verify_provision` degrades the confirmation to a single signal computed from the receipt in hand: green, this is the good that was sovereignly provisioned; amber, it is not. A change to the good or the receipt flips the light. The person least equipped to audit a good — a family member, a neighbor, a buyer — is handed the same certainty as the provisioner. Sovereignty you cannot check is sovereignty you do not hold; a good's receipt means the weakest receiver can check. **It composes the sealed floors and names its boundary -- the Object Model, provenance, mandate, and the human gate, with economic value, estate, and the verticals homed to their own series -- so every guarantee has a stated, checkable home.** The fifth pillar is honesty about the boundary. The primitive borrows its governed object from the Object Model (S5 Vol 5), its provenance from P5, its scope from the mandate (S5 Vol 28), and its human gate from the HumanApprovalGate (S5 Vol 16); economic value homes OUT to Sovereign Economy (S10), the material estate to Generational Transfer (S12), and energy, food and water, shelter, logistics, and the covenant to S9 Vols 2–6. The opener owns exactly one thing — the material provision — and points everything else at its real home. Nothing floats. **With this volume the material layer opens -- provision, and the verticals to come stand on it -- a node sovereign not only in its records but in the goods it holds.** This is the first volume of Material Sovereignty. The sovereign layer now reaches from data into matter: a node's records were made receipted, governed, and verifiable across five series, and now its physical goods are too, beginning with the primitive that provisions them. Energy, food and water, shelter, logistics, and the covenant that binds them all stand on this — a good provisioned as a receipted, locally-held, human-gated, receipt-verifiable object. Matter joins data under one sovereignty. **The generational payoff is a good a receiver can hold AND verify -- not a thing they must trust -- because provisioning itself is now sovereign and checkable by the weakest party.** Lasting Generational Prosperity asks that what is built and provisioned passes on intact and confirmable. A node's goods are among the most tangible things it hands on, and until now their proof lived in a provider's registry. This volume makes them pass on as governed objects with portable receipts: a receiver inherits a good they can hold and confirm from its receipt alone. Provisioning stops being a reference to someone else's database and becomes the holder's verifiable possession. The good survives its provisioner — held, gated, and verifiable by whoever comes next. **In the acceptance tests, a good provisions as a receipted object, holds in the node's own registry, gates on a human, and verifies by receipt -- so the material-primitive discipline is executable and proven, and the material layer opens on runnable proof, not assertion.** The eleven tests of `test_provision_local.py` prove every claim of this volume, and the whole kernel suite stays green around them. For the Ridgeline homestead, the primitive means every good it provisions — a panel, a pump, a harvest — is a governed object it holds on its own storage, stands behind with a human, and hands on with a receipt any receiver can verify. This is the material layer's first word: a node whose matter is as sovereign as its records — a good you can hold and verify, not merely trust. That is the foundation of a prosperity meant to last.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
text: You will see why a sovereign node's energy must be metered and provisioned as receipted, verifiable governed objects -- held locally, metered honestly, checkable by whoever receives them -- rather than billed by a central utility a node cannot audit, so power can be metered and verified, not merely trusted.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
text: **The opener made a physical good a receipted governed object a node holds and verifies; this volume points that primitive at energy -- the power a node generates, stores, and hands on.** The Material Primitive made any good sovereign: receipted, mandate-scoped, held locally, verifiable by receipt. Energy is a good like any other, and this volume provisions it exactly so. A kilowatt-hour becomes a governed object with a receipt, not a number on someone else's bill. **A kilowatt-hour is usually a number on a utility's bill -- metered by a device the node does not own, recorded in a registry it cannot audit.** This is how energy is normally accounted: by the utility. The meter belongs to the provider, the reading lives in the provider's system, and the node holding the panel and the battery does not hold the record of what it generated. To know its own production, it reads a bill. The most physical output a node has — the power it makes — is measured and recorded by a party it neither owns nor can inspect. **Energy verifiable only by a utility's registry is energy you do not fully hold -- the reading depends on a meter and a system you do not control, and it can change without you.** This is the energy failure. If the only record of a generation is a row in a utility's database, then the utility controls the truth about the node's own power. The reading can be revised, disputed, or lost, and the node has no independent record to check it against. Sovereignty over power you cannot verify without the utility's permission is not sovereignty; it is metered dependence. **The sovereign opportunity is to meter and provision energy as a receipted, mandate-scoped governed object the node holds itself -- the Material Primitive applied to power.** This volume builds that. `provision_energy` provisions a metered quantity of energy — a generation or a stored amount, from a named asset over a period — as a governed object in the node's own registry, through the Material Primitive (S9 Vol 1). The kilowatt-hour becomes a receipted object the node holds, not a line on a bill. The opener built the harness; this points it at energy. **There is no central utility and the metering is honest -- each node meters and provisions its own energy locally, and a reading cannot be negative or absent.** Two disciplines guard the primitive. No central utility: `provision_energy` writes into the node's own registry, not a shared one, so no node depends on a utility it does not control. And honest metering: a reading must be a real, non-negative quantity — a negative or absent reading is refused — so the meter cannot record an impossible generation. The power is metered locally, honestly. **The weakest-party stake is a receiver who can verify a metered amount by a green light -- from the energy's receipt alone, no utility registry, no expertise.** Lasting Generational Prosperity asks that what a node produces can be confirmed by whoever receives it. `verify_energy` gives exactly that: it re-derives the energy good's receipt and checks the metered amount, returning a plain verified-or-tampered verdict. A person handed energy — or an energy credit — and its receipt confirms it is the amount that was sovereignly metered, with no call to a utility and no expertise. The chapters build the discipline: the metered good (Ch 2), no central utility (Ch 3), honest metering (Ch 4), and verify-by-receipt (Ch 5), with what it composes (Ch 6), the contrast with the utility meter (Ch 7), and the synthesis (Ch 8).

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: provision_energy -- Metered Generation as a Receipted Good
text: You will see how a metered quantity of energy becomes a governed object -- provision_energy provisions it as a receipted, mandate-scoped version in the node's registry, keyed to an asset and a period -- so a kilowatt-hour you generate carries the same verifiable receipt as any good you hold.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: provision_energy -- Metered Generation as a Receipted Good
text: **A verifiable kilowatt-hour begins with one governed object and one honest receipt -- the generation is provisioned as a Material Primitive good, hash-chained and mandate-scoped, keyed to an asset and a period.** Before energy can be verified it must be provisioned as a governed object. This chapter builds that. `provision_energy` takes a metered quantity — an asset, a number of kilowatt-hours, a period — and provisions it through the Material Primitive (S9 Vol 1) as a receipted version. The generation becomes an object the node governs, and the version it produces is its receipt. **`provision_energy(asset, kwh, *, period, mandate, author, source_ref, at, registry)` provisions the metered quantity as a receipted good -- one call, one governed object, and the version it returns is the energy's receipt.** The signature is the whole idea. Given an asset, a reading in kilowatt-hours, a period, a mandate, a provenance-checked source, a stated time, and the node's registry, `provision_energy` provisions the generation and returns it. `test_provisions_metered_energy_as_receipted_object` proves it: the receipt carries `kind: provision`, the mandate, the kilowatt-hours, the unit, and the period. The kilowatt-hour is now a governed object with a receipt — not a line on a bill. **The generation's identity is its asset and its period -- a rooftop array in a given month is `MaterialGood:<asset>@<period>`, one governed object, not a re-countable figure.** Identity is content, not a running total. `provision_energy` keys the good's identity on the asset and the period — `MaterialGood:rooftop-array-01@2026-08` — so a generation period is one object. A kilowatt-hour figure is not a number that can be silently re-counted; it is a named object for a named asset over a named period. This is what lets a receipt be checked and not double-counted: the identity binds the reading to exactly one asset and one span of time. **The good carries the reading, the unit, and the period -- so the receipt states exactly what was metered, in what unit, over what span, with nothing implicit.** The energy good is explicit. It records the kilowatt-hours, the unit (`kWh`), and the period, so the receipt is self-describing: a receiver reads not a bare number but a metered quantity, unit-typed, for a stated period. There is no implicit unit to misread and no ambiguous span. What was metered is exactly what the receipt says. **The version is hash-chained, mandate-scoped, and provenance-checked -- provision_energy composes the Material Primitive, so the generation inherits the primitive's integrity, scope, and honest citation.** The primitive does the governance. Because `provision_energy` provisions through `provision_local`, the generation is hash-chained (tamper-evident), bound to exactly one mandate (S5 Vol 28), and carries a source that must resolve (P5). The energy volume adds the metering; the integrity, scope, and provenance are the sealed primitive's, composed. A generation record is as governed as any record the node keeps. **The receipt is the slip that travels with the energy -- a portable, verifiable record a receiver can hold, not a lookup into a utility they cannot reach.** The point of a receipt is that it moves. When Ridgeline provisions a month's generation, the version `provision_energy` returns is a self-contained record — asset, kilowatt-hours, unit, period, mandate, hash — that can travel with the energy or an energy credit to whoever receives it. The receiver does not need the utility's system to check it; they hold the receipt. Provenance travels with the power. **One generation, one receipted governed object -- the metering harness that made a good verifiable, now holding energy, which is the foundation the rest of the volume builds on.** The result is power governed like a record: metered, receipted, hash-chained, mandate-scoped. That is what makes the deeper guarantees possible — because the generation is a governed object with a portable receipt, it can be metered locally with no central utility (Chapter 3), metered honestly (Chapter 4), and verified by its receipt (Chapter 5). The generation is one; its receipt travels; its governance is the primitive's. **In the acceptance tests, a metered generation provisions as a receipted object with its asset, reading, unit, and period -- so the metered-good discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_provisions_metered_energy_as_receipted_object` proves the receipt's shape and content. For the Ridgeline homestead, this means a month of rooftop generation is provisioned as `MaterialGood:rooftop-array-01@2026-08`, a hash-chained object under the homestead's mandate, with a receipt the energy carries. Chapter 3 shows why that registry is the homestead's own — and why there is no central utility in the loop.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: No Central Utility -- Each Node Meters Its Own
text: You will see the first discipline that makes provisioned energy sovereign -- provision_energy writes into the node's OWN local registry, never a central utility -- so no node depends on a utility it does not control, and its power is held, not merely billed.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: No Central Utility -- Each Node Meters Its Own
text: **Sovereignly provisioned energy is metered and held by the node itself -- provision_energy writes into the node's own registry, so there is no central utility any node depends on.** The danger with energy is the utility: a single provider every node must go through to meter, record, or confirm its power. This chapter refuses it. `provision_energy` takes the node's own registry and writes there — inheriting the Material Primitive's no-central-provisioner discipline, now applied to power. Each node meters into the registry it holds. **The registry is the node's own -- provision_energy takes it as a parameter and writes there, so a generation is recorded where the node holds it, not in a utility's database across a network.** The locality is explicit in the signature. `provision_energy` knows about no central meter store; it writes to the registry the caller passes, the node's own. A generation is recorded where the panel and the battery are. There is no moment where the node must reach a utility to make a reading real. **Two nodes meter independently into their own registries -- each generation lives only in the node that produced it, with no shared registry either depends on.** The primitive scales by not sharing. `test_no_central_utility_two_local_registries` proves it: Ridgeline provisions its array's output into its registry and Cedar provisions its turbine's into its own; each generation lives in exactly one node's registry, and neither node's metering touches the other's store. Two sovereign nodes generating power are two independent holders, not two accounts on one utility. **A receipt from one node still verifies at another -- because verify_energy checks the receipt itself, a generation metered at one node is confirmable at any node, with no shared utility.** Locality of metering does not mean isolation of proof. Although each generation lives only in its own node's registry, its receipt is portable: `test_no_central_utility_two_local_registries` proves one node's generation verifies from its receipt alone at another. `verify_energy` needs no utility registry at all. So power is metered locally and proofs travel freely — with no central utility that all metering depends on. **No central utility is what keeps metering sovereign -- there is no single system whose outage, capture, or revision breaks every node's ability to meter or confirm its power.** A central utility is a single point of failure and control. If every reading had to be recorded in one system, that system's outage would halt settlement everywhere, its compromise would corrupt every node's generation records, and its operator would hold power over all of them. By writing to each node's own registry, `provision_energy` removes that point. There is nothing to capture that would break the whole; each node's metering stands on its own. **Local metering mirrors the sovereignty of local records and goods -- a node holds its energy as it holds its records, on its own storage, under its own mandate, answerable to no central authority.** The primitive is consistent with the whole stack. A sovereign node keeps its records and its goods on its own storage under its own mandate; now it keeps its energy the same way. There is no more a central power authority than there is a central records authority. Ridgeline's kilowatt-hours are Ridgeline's — metered, provisioned, and governed locally. Power joins data and matter under one sovereignty. **Energy held locally with a portable receipt is both sovereign and settleable -- the node depends on no utility, and any counterparty can still verify, which the rest of the volume builds on.** The result is metering that is neither centralized nor siloed. A generation is held by exactly one node, dependent on no external utility, and yet its receipt lets any counterparty confirm it. Because metering is local and the receipt is portable, the reading can be honest by construction (Chapter 4) and the weakest receiver can verify it (Chapter 5). Held locally; provable anywhere. **In the acceptance tests, two nodes meter into their own registries and each verifies the other's generation by receipt -- so the no-central-utility discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_no_central_utility_two_local_registries` proves the independent local registries and the cross-node verification by receipt. For Ridgeline and its neighbor Cedar, this means each homestead meters its own power on its own storage, and either can confirm the other's generation from the receipt that travels with it — no shared utility. Chapter 4 makes the metering honest.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: Honest Metering -- A Reading That Cannot Be Faked
text: You will see the discipline that makes a metered reading trustworthy -- a reading must be a real, non-negative quantity, and any change to it flips verification to tampered -- so a generation cannot be inflated, faked, or negative, and the number on the receipt is the number that was metered.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: Honest Metering -- A Reading That Cannot Be Faked
text: **Honest metering means a reading is a real, non-negative quantity -- provision_energy refuses a negative or absent reading, so the meter cannot record an impossible generation.** A record is only as trustworthy as the reading behind it. This chapter builds the guard that fits a meter. `provision_energy` refuses a reading that is negative or absent — a generation cannot be less than zero, and a missing figure is not a reading. The number that enters the receipt is a real quantity, or the provision does not happen. **A negative or absent reading is refused -- provision_energy fails closed on an impossible generation, so a meter cannot record power that was never made.** The guard is fail-closed. `test_negative_meter_reading_refused` proves it: a negative reading raises before anything is recorded. A generation is a non-negative quantity by physical fact, and the primitive enforces that fact — a negative or missing figure is not provisioned, so no impossible reading ever enters a receipt. The meter records what could have been generated, or it records nothing. **The reading is unit-typed and bound into the receipt -- so a number cannot be read in the wrong unit or detached from its asset and period.** Honesty is also about clarity. The reading is stored with its unit and bound to its asset and period in the hash-chained receipt. A figure cannot be quietly reinterpreted in a different unit, or lifted from one asset's record and attached to another's — the receipt binds the number, the unit, the asset, and the period together. What was metered is unambiguous. **A reading inflated or altered after the fact flips verification to tampered -- because the receipt is hash-chained, a changed number does not re-derive.** The strongest guarantee is tamper-evidence. `test_verify_energy_detects_a_tampered_reading` proves it: a receipt whose kilowatt-hours are inflated after provisioning fails to verify. Because the reading is part of the hash-chained receipt, any change to it — an inflation, a downward revision, a swap — is detectable, and `verify_energy` flips to tampered. A generation figure cannot be quietly edited to claim more power than was made; the receipt either re-derives with the real number or fails. **Honest metering matters because energy settles into value -- an inflated reading is not a harmless error but a false claim on what the power is worth, which is why the guard is strict.** It matters that this lands on energy. A kilowatt-hour is not just a number; it settles into economic value (homed to Sovereign Economy, S10) and into what a node can hand on. An inflated reading is a false claim on that value. Refusing impossible readings and catching altered ones is not fussiness — it is what keeps a generation record from becoming a way to claim power that was never produced. The strictness is proportionate to the stake. **The metering guard composes the primitive's integrity -- provision_energy adds the non-negativity check, and the hash-chained tamper-evidence is the Material Primitive's, so honesty is layered, not re-implemented.** The primitive rolls no new integrity. `provision_energy` adds exactly one domain guard — a reading is non-negative — and inherits the tamper-evidence from the Material Primitive's hash-chained receipt. So an honest reading is guarded twice: at entry (non-negative) and forever after (tamper-evident), the second borrowed from the sealed floor. The energy volume contributes the physical honesty of a meter; the cryptographic honesty is the primitive's, composed. **A reading that cannot be faked or altered is a generation a node can stand behind -- which the receiver, and the value it settles into, can rely on.** The result is a metered figure trustworthy at both ends: it could not have been impossible when recorded, and it cannot have been changed since. A receiver checking a generation's receipt reads the number that was actually metered. That is what makes energy safe to settle and to hand on: the reading is honest by construction and honest forever. Chapter 5 shows how any receiver — even the weakest — verifies all of this from the receipt alone. **In the acceptance tests, a negative reading is refused and a tampered reading fails verification -- so the honest-metering discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_negative_meter_reading_refused` proves the fail-closed guard, and `test_verify_energy_detects_a_tampered_reading` proves the tamper-evidence. For Ridgeline, this means a month's generation cannot be recorded as an impossible figure and cannot be inflated after the fact — the number on the receipt is the number the array made. Chapter 5 turns the receipt into a green light the weakest receiver can read.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: Verify by Receipt -- A Green Light on Every Kilowatt-Hour
text: You will see how a provisioned generation becomes verifiable to the weakest receiver -- verify_energy re-derives the receipt and confirms the metered amount, returning a green light with no utility registry -- so a resourceless person confirms a kilowatt-hour is sovereignly metered, no second device, no expertise.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: Verify by Receipt -- A Green Light on Every Kilowatt-Hour
text: **A verifiable kilowatt-hour is one you can check from its receipt alone -- verify_energy re-derives the energy good's receipt and confirms the metered amount, with no utility registry and no second device.** A receipt that can only be checked against a utility is no better than the utility. This chapter builds the check that needs neither. `verify_energy` takes the receipt and the metered facts — asset, kilowatt-hours, period — and returns a verdict: verified if the receipt re-derives and the amount matches, tampered if not, using only what the receiver holds. **`verify_energy(receipt, asset, kwh, *, period)` returns verified when the receipt re-derives and the amount matches, tampered when either fails -- one signal, computed from the receipt itself.** The signature is the whole idea. `test_verify_energy_by_receipt_no_registry` proves that a receiver holding only the receipt and the metered facts gets `provisioned: True` with reason "provisioned" — no utility passed, none needed. The verdict is a plain boolean with a reason, not a bill to interpret. A person reads one signal: is this the kilowatt-hour that was sovereignly metered? Green, yes. Amber, something is wrong. **The check re-derives the receipt via the Material Primitive -- so it composes the primitive's integrity and rolls no cryptography of its own.** The verification reuses the floor. `verify_energy` rebuilds the canonical energy good and passes it to the primitive's `verify_provision`, which re-derives the receipt's hash from its own fields and compares. This is the Material Primitive's hashing, composed — `verify_energy` rolls no cryptography itself. The check answers "does this receipt re-derive?" using the exact machinery that produced it. **A change to the reading, asset, or period flips the verdict to tampered -- an inflated kilowatt-hour, a swapped asset, a shifted period all fail, so a generation cannot be quietly restated.** The guarantee is that tampering shows. Because the energy good binds the reading, asset, and period, `verify_energy` fails on any divergence: a receiver cannot be told a different figure than the receipt metered, or shown a receipt altered to claim a different asset or month. `test_verify_energy_detects_a_tampered_reading` proves the reading case. A generation cannot be quietly restated to claim more. **The check is weakest-party verifiable -- no utility registry, no second device, no expertise -- so the person least equipped to audit a generation can still confirm it is sovereignly metered.** This is the standing lens of the sovereign layer, on power. Sovereignty you cannot check is sovereignty you do not hold — and a person receiving energy should not need a utility login or a specialist to confirm it. `verify_energy` degrades the check to a single signal from the receipt in hand. A recipient with no access to the metering node, no second machine, and no technical skill still answers the only question that matters — is this the kilowatt-hour that was metered? The weakest receiver is handed the same certainty as the producer. **Verify-by-receipt is what makes a locally-metered generation universally checkable -- the energy stays with its node, but its proof travels to whoever holds the receipt.** This closes the circle. Because the receipt carries everything and `verify_energy` needs nothing else, a generation metered at one node (Chapter 3) is confirmable by anyone who receives its receipt. The reading was honest by construction (Chapter 4); the receiver sees the real figure. Local metering and universal verifiability coexist precisely because the check is against the receipt, not a utility. **A generation verifiable by its own receipt is power you meter and verify -- metered locally, metered honestly, and confirmable by the weakest receiver, which is what the whole primitive was for.** The result is the promise of the volume, made checkable. A kilowatt-hour is metered as a receipted governed object, held by its node, honest by construction, and verifiable by whoever receives it — all without a central utility anyone must trust. A receiver does not take the reading on faith; they read its light. Chapter 6 names exactly what this primitive composes and what it homes out. **In the acceptance tests, a generation verifies by receipt with no registry, and a tampered reading flips to tampered -- so the verify-by-receipt, weakest-party discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_verify_energy_by_receipt_no_registry` and `test_verify_energy_detects_a_tampered_reading` prove the cases. For Ridgeline, this means anyone the homestead settles energy with — a neighbor, a buyer, an heir — can confirm from the receipt alone that a generation is the amount the homestead sovereignly metered, with no call to a utility and no expertise. Chapter 6 draws the map of composed floors.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: What Sovereign Energy Composes -- The Material Primitive and the Meter
text: You will see exactly what this primitive builds on and what it deliberately leaves out -- it composes the Material Primitive (and through it the Object Model, mandate, and human gate) and adds the meter, homing economic value and estate to their own series -- so the boundary is drawn as precisely as its center.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: What Sovereign Energy Composes -- The Material Primitive and the Meter
text: **A domain volume is defined by what it composes -- Sovereign Energy stands on the Material Primitive and adds exactly one thing: an honest meter.** The second volume of the series is a composition. This chapter draws the map. `provision_energy` builds on the Material Primitive for the governed object, the local holding, the human gate, and the by-receipt verification — and it adds one new thing, the metering of energy. Naming the composition is how the volume stays honest about where each guarantee lives. **It composes the Material Primitive (S9 Vol 1) -- every metered generation is a receipted, locally-held, human-gated, receipt-verifiable good, so energy inherits all of the opener's guarantees.** The primitive is the foundation. `provision_energy` provisions through `provision_local`, and `verify_energy` verifies through `verify_provision`. The receipted governed object, the no-central-provisioner locality, the human gate, the verify-by-receipt — all of it comes from the Material Primitive. The energy volume does not rebuild the harness; it points it at power. **Through the primitive it composes the Object Model, the mandate, and the human gate -- so energy is hash-chained, scoped to one mandate, and gated by a human exactly as any good is.** The deeper floors travel with the primitive. Because it composes the Material Primitive, `provision_energy` inherits the Object Model's hashing (S5 Vol 5), the mandate scope (S5 Vol 28), and the HumanApprovalGate (S5 Vol 16). `test_human_primacy_gated_energy_refused_without_approval` proves a gated energy provision is refused without a human. Energy is governed by the same floors as records and goods, borrowed through one composition. **It owns exactly one thing -- the meter -- an honest, non-negative, unit-typed, period-scoped reading provisioned as a receipted good.** What the volume adds is the metering. `provision_energy` contributes the physical honesty of a reading (non-negative), its unit typing, its period scope, and its identity keyed to an asset and a span. That — and only that — is the energy volume's own. Everything else is composed. The claim is small and exact: the meter, on top of the primitive. **It homes the energy's economic value OUT to Sovereign Economy (S10) and its material estate to Generational Transfer (S12) -- the primitive meters the power, it does not price it or inherit it.** The honest boundary. A metered generation has an economic value — what it is worth, how it settles or trades — and that homes OUT to Sovereign Economy (Series 10). A generation is also part of an estate that passes on, and that homes to Generational Transfer (Series 12). `provision_energy` meters and verifies the power; it does not price it, trade it, or inherit it. **Drawing the boundary precisely is what makes the volume trustworthy -- it claims exactly the meter, composes its guarantees from named sealed floors, and points every other concern at its real home.** The value of the map is that nothing floats. The governed object, locality, gate, and verification are the Material Primitive's (and through it the Object Model's, the mandate's, and the compliance gate's). Economic value is S10's, estate is S12's. What is left for this volume is the meter: an honest, receipted, verifiable reading. A domain volume that names its boundary this precisely is one a reader can trust exactly. **In the composition, Sovereign Energy owns the meter and cites the rest by their series-qualified homes -- so the volume is a precise assembly, not a monolith.** The receipt of this chapter is the map itself: Material Primitive (S9 V1), Object Model (S5 V5), mandate (S5 V28), human gate (S5 V16); economic value OUT to S10, estate OUT to S12. For Ridgeline, the homestead's energy is metered by a primitive that borrows its governance from the volumes it already trusts, and points the value and the inheritance of that power to where they belong. Chapter 7 sets the whole thing against the utility meter.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: Sovereign Energy vs the Utility Meter
text: You will see the two approaches set side by side -- power metered by a utility a node cannot audit versus power metered as a locally-held, receipt-verifiable governed object -- so the sovereign choice between them is explicit, not implied.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
chapter_title: Sovereign Energy vs the Utility Meter
text: **The choice is between power you are billed for and power you hold -- a utility's meter reading versus a locally-held receipted generation -- and the difference is whether a node controls the truth about its own energy.** Every node accounts for its power somehow; the question is whether the truth lives in a system it controls. This chapter sets the two side by side. The utility meter keeps the truth in the provider's device and database. Sovereign Energy keeps it in the node's own registry, in a receipt that travels with the energy. The contrast is the argument of the whole volume. **The utility meter keeps the truth in a device and database the node cannot audit -- the node reads a bill it does not control, and confirmation means trusting the provider.** A utility meter is a reading, not a holding. The device belongs to the provider, the number lives in the provider's system, and the node holding the panel cannot audit either. To confirm what it generated, the node reads a bill and trusts it. The truth about the node's own power lives outside the node. **Sovereign Energy keeps the truth in the node's own registry and the generation's own receipt -- the node holds the reading and confirms it without asking anyone.** The sovereign answer moves the truth home. `provision_energy` records the generation in the node's own registry, and the receipt carries its own proof. The node holds the reading and can confirm it — or hand a counterparty the means to confirm it — without querying any utility. The truth lives where the power was made. **The utility record can change without the node -- a reading can be revised or disputed, and the node has no independent record -- while the primitive's receipt re-derives or fails.** With a utility, the record is the provider's to alter or dispute. A reading can be revised, a bill contested, and the node has no independent copy to check against. With the primitive, the receipt is hash-chained: it either re-derives or it does not, and any alteration shows as tampered. A record someone else can quietly change versus one that cannot be changed invisibly. **The utility meter requires trust to confirm a generation -- while the primitive's receipt is verifiable by the weakest counterparty with no access at all.** A utility serves those it bills. To confirm a generation, you read the provider's number and trust it. The primitive lowers that to nothing: `verify_energy` checks the receipt in hand, so a counterparty with no access to any system and no expertise still confirms the amount. Verifiability by anyone who holds the receipt replaces verifiability by the meter's owner. **Choosing Sovereign Energy is a sovereign choice -- it is what lets a node control the truth about its own power, held and verifiable rather than billed and trusted.** This is the sovereignty frame. Power known only through a utility's meter is power the node does not fully own — the provider controls its record and its confirmation. Power metered as a locally-held, receipt-verifiable object is owned in full: held on the node's storage, under its mandate, honest by construction, confirmable without permission. The sovereign asset is not the utility's reading; it is the generation you hold and the receipt you can verify. **The contrast is not convenience versus features -- it is billed-and-trusted versus held-and-verifiable, which for a node's own power is the whole game.** It would be easy to read this as a nicer energy dashboard. It is not. The utility meter and Sovereign Energy differ on the one axis that matters: whether the node controls the truth about its own power. A node whose generation can be revised or disputed by a provider it cannot audit does not sovereignly hold its energy, however slick the app. Sovereign Energy makes power sovereign by making it held and verifiable. Chapter 8 draws the primitive together. **In the composition of the whole volume, Sovereign Energy is what the utility meter cannot be -- metered honestly, held locally, and verifiable by anyone -- which is why it is the second brick of the material layer.** The receipt of this chapter is the contrast itself, pointing back to the runnable proof: `provision_energy` meters honestly and locally, and `verify_energy` confirms by receipt — properties a utility reading structurally lacks. For Ridgeline, adopting Sovereign Energy means the power it makes is confirmable by every counterparty and successor, not trusted from a bill. Chapter 8 closes the volume.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
text: You will see the whole volume drawn together -- a generation metered as a receipted governed object, held locally with no central utility, metered honestly, and verifiable by receipt -- and with it the material layer's second brick: the sovereign discipline of goods extended to power.

title: S9 02 Sovereign Energy
text: **Sovereign Energy makes present one thing -- a metered generation provisioned as a receipted, mandate-scoped governed object a node holds, meters honestly, and can verify by receipt -- and that one thing is the material layer's second brick.** The opener made a good sovereign; this volume makes power sovereign. `provision_energy` provisions a metered generation as a governed object in the node's own registry; the reading is honest by construction; `verify_energy` confirms it from its receipt alone. A kilowatt-hour becomes as held and verifiable as a record — which is what Material Sovereignty reaches toward: not just goods you can hold, but power you can meter and prove. **The generation is metered as a receipted governed object -- hash-chained, mandate-scoped, provenance-true -- so a kilowatt-hour carries the same verifiable receipt as any good.** The first pillar is the governed object. `provision_energy` composes the Material Primitive to provision a generation as a hash-chained version bound to one mandate, keyed to an asset and a period. Its receipt travels with the energy and re-derives or fails. Power inherits the exact integrity goods and records hold. **It is held locally with no central utility -- each node meters into its own registry, so no node depends on a utility it does not control, and yet a receipt verifies anywhere.** The second pillar is local holding. `provision_energy` writes into the node's own registry; two nodes meter independently; and a receipt from one verifies at another by receipt alone. There is no central utility whose outage, capture, or revision breaks the whole. Power is metered where it is made, and its proof travels. **The metering is honest -- a reading cannot be negative or absent, and an inflated or altered reading fails verification -- so a generation cannot claim power that was never made.** The third pillar is the meter. `provision_energy` refuses impossible readings at capture and binds the reading into a tamper-evident receipt, so a figure cannot be faked or later inflated. The number on the receipt is the number the asset made — honest at entry and honest forever. **The check is weakest-party verifiable -- verify_energy re-derives the receipt and confirms the amount, so a resourceless receiver reads a green light with no utility registry, no second device, no expertise.** The fourth pillar makes power universally trustworthy. `verify_energy` degrades the confirmation to a single signal computed from the receipt in hand: green, this is the kilowatt-hour that was sovereignly metered; amber, it is not. A change to the reading, asset, or period flips the light. The person least equipped to audit a generation is handed the same certainty as the producer. Sovereignty you cannot check is sovereignty you do not hold. **It composes the sealed floors and names its boundary -- the Material Primitive and its governance, with economic value and estate homed to their own series -- so every guarantee has a stated, checkable home.** The fifth pillar is honesty about the boundary. The primitive borrows its governed object, locality, gate, and verification from the Material Primitive (S9 Vol 1), and through it the Object Model (S5 Vol 5), the mandate (S5 Vol 28), and the human gate (S5 Vol 16); economic value homes OUT to Sovereign Economy (S10) and the material estate to Generational Transfer (S12). The volume owns exactly one thing — the meter — and points everything else at its real home. Nothing floats. **With this volume the material layer gains its energy brick -- meter, on top of provision -- a node sovereign not only in its goods but in the power it makes.** This is the second volume of Material Sovereignty. A node's records, rules, surface, and goods were made sovereign; now its energy is too. Food and water, shelter, logistics, and the covenant that binds them will each stand on the same primitive, metered or measured, held and verified. Power joins matter under one sovereignty. **The generational payoff is power a receiver can meter AND verify -- not a bill they must trust -- because metering itself is now sovereign and checkable by the weakest party.** Lasting Generational Prosperity asks that what a node produces passes on intact and confirmable. A node's energy is among the most tangible things it produces, and until now its proof lived in a utility's database. This volume makes it pass on as a governed object with a portable receipt: a receiver inherits power they can meter and confirm from its receipt alone. Metering stops being a reference to a utility and becomes the holder's verifiable possession. **In the acceptance tests, a generation provisions as a receipted object, holds in the node's own registry, meters honestly, and verifies by receipt -- so the energy-primitive discipline is executable and proven, and the energy brick lands on runnable proof, not assertion.** The eight tests of `test_provision_energy.py` prove every claim of this volume, and the whole kernel suite stays green around them. For the Ridgeline homestead, the primitive means every kilowatt-hour it makes is a governed object it holds on its own storage, meters honestly, and hands on with a receipt any receiver can verify. This is the energy brick's word: a node whose power is as sovereign as its goods — power you meter and verify, not a bill you trust. That is the foundation of a prosperity meant to last.

title: S9 03 Food Water
text: You will see why a sovereign node's food and water must be provisioned as receipted, traceable governed objects -- held locally, origin-bound, checkable by whoever receives them -- rather than labeled in an opaque supply chain a node cannot audit, so sustenance can be traced and verified, not merely trusted.

title: S9 03 Food Water
text: **The opener made a physical good a receipted governed object a node holds and verifies; this volume points that primitive at sustenance -- the food and water a node grows, stores, and hands on.** The Material Primitive made any good sovereign: receipted, mandate-scoped, held locally, verifiable by receipt. Food and water are goods like any other, and this volume provisions them exactly so — with one addition the domain demands: a traceable origin. A bushel or a tank becomes a governed object with a receipt and a known source, not a labeled line in someone else's supply chain. **A food or water good is usually a line in an opaque supply chain -- its origin a label you trust, tracked in a distributor's system the node cannot audit.** This is how sustenance is normally accounted. The good exists, its origin is a printed claim, and the record of it lives in a distributor's or retailer's system. The node holding the food does not hold the record of where it came from; to trust the origin, it reads a label. The most vital good a node holds — what it eats and drinks — carries a provenance it cannot independently confirm. **Sustenance whose origin is only a label is sustenance you cannot fully trust -- the origin depends on a chain you do not control, and it can be mislabeled or lost.** This is the sustenance failure. If the only proof of where a food came from is a label and a distributor's row, then the chain — not the holder — controls the truth about it. The origin can be mislabeled, substituted, or lost, and the node has no independent way to confirm it. Trust in food you cannot trace is trust you have extended on someone else's word. **The sovereign opportunity is to provision sustenance as a receipted, mandate-scoped governed object with a required traceable origin the node holds itself -- the Material Primitive, with provenance made mandatory.** This volume builds that. `provision_sustenance` provisions a food or water good — a quantity, of a kind, from an origin — as a governed object in the node's own registry, through the Material Primitive (S9 Vol 1), and it refuses a good with no traceable origin. The bushel becomes a receipted object the node holds, with its source bound in. The opener built the harness; this points it at sustenance and makes origin non-optional. **There is no central provisioner and the origin is required -- each node provisions its own sustenance locally, and a food or water good without a traceable origin is refused.** Two disciplines guard the primitive. No central provisioner: `provision_sustenance` writes into the node's own registry, so no node depends on a chain it does not control. And a required origin: a food or water good must name where it came from — regenerative provenance is not optional — and one without it is refused. The sustenance is provisioned locally, with its source bound in. **The weakest-party stake is a receiver who can verify a good and its origin by a green light -- from the sustenance's receipt alone, no registry, no expertise.** Lasting Generational Prosperity asks that what a node provides can be confirmed by whoever receives it. `verify_sustenance` gives exactly that: it re-derives the good's receipt and checks both the good and its origin, returning a plain verified-or-tampered verdict. A person handed food or water and its receipt confirms it is the good that was sovereignly provisioned, from the origin it claims — with no call to a chain and no expertise. The chapters build the discipline: the traceable good (Ch 2), no central provisioner (Ch 3), the required origin (Ch 4), and verify-by-receipt (Ch 5), with what it composes (Ch 6), the contrast with the supply chain (Ch 7), and the synthesis (Ch 8).

title: S9 03 Food Water
chapter_title: provision_sustenance -- Food & Water as a Receipted Good with an Origin
text: You will see how a food or water good becomes a governed object -- provision_sustenance provisions it as a receipted, mandate-scoped version keyed to its kind, item, and origin -- so a harvest you hold carries the same verifiable receipt as any good, with its source bound in.

title: S9 03 Food Water
chapter_title: provision_sustenance -- Food & Water as a Receipted Good with an Origin
text: **A traceable food good begins with one governed object and one honest receipt -- the good is provisioned as a Material Primitive good, hash-chained and mandate-scoped, keyed to its kind, item, and origin.** Before sustenance can be traced it must be provisioned as a governed object with its source bound in. This chapter builds that. `provision_sustenance` takes a food or water item — a quantity, a kind, an origin — and provisions it through the Material Primitive (S9 Vol 1) as a receipted version whose identity includes the origin. The harvest becomes an object the node governs, and the version it produces is its receipt. **`provision_sustenance(item, quantity, *, kind_of, origin, mandate, ...)` provisions the good as a receipted object -- one call, one governed object, and the version it returns is the sustenance's receipt.** The signature is the whole idea. Given an item, a quantity, a kind (food or water), an origin, a mandate, a provenance-checked source, and the node's registry, `provision_sustenance` provisions the good and returns it. `test_provisions_sustenance_as_receipted_object` proves it: the receipt carries `kind: provision`, the mandate, the quantity, the kind, and the origin. The harvest is now a governed object with a receipt — not a labeled line in a chain. **The good's identity includes its origin -- a food or water good is `MaterialGood:<kind>:<item>:<origin>`, so provenance is part of what the object IS, not a detachable label.** Identity is content, and here content includes source. `provision_sustenance` keys the good's identity on kind, item, and origin — `MaterialGood:food:heirloom-wheat:north-field-2026` — so the origin is bound into the object's very identity. A good's provenance is not a sticker that can be peeled off and replaced; it is part of the object. This is what makes the origin verifiable: it is in the good, not on it. **The good carries the quantity, the unit, the kind, and the origin -- so the receipt states exactly what was provisioned, how much, of what kind, from where, with nothing implicit.** The sustenance good is explicit. It records the quantity, unit, kind (food or water), and origin, so the receipt is self-describing: a receiver reads not a bare label but a governed good with a stated quantity, kind, and source. There is no implicit provenance to trust. What was provisioned, and where it came from, is exactly what the receipt says. **The version is hash-chained, mandate-scoped, and provenance-checked -- provision_sustenance composes the Material Primitive, so the good inherits the primitive's integrity, scope, and honest citation.** The primitive does the governance. Because `provision_sustenance` provisions through `provision_local`, the good is hash-chained (tamper-evident), bound to exactly one mandate (S5 Vol 28), and carries a source that must resolve (P5). The sustenance volume adds the origin requirement; the integrity, scope, and provenance rule are the sealed primitive's, composed. A harvest record is as governed as any record the node keeps. **The receipt is the slip that travels with the food -- a portable, verifiable record a receiver can hold, not a lookup into a chain they cannot reach.** The point of a receipt is that it moves. When Ridgeline provisions a harvest, the version `provision_sustenance` returns is a self-contained record — item, quantity, kind, origin, mandate, hash — that can travel with the food to whoever receives it. The receiver does not need the distributor's system to check where it came from; they hold the receipt. Provenance travels with the food, bound in. **One good, one receipted governed object with its origin bound in -- the harness that made a good verifiable, now holding sustenance, which is the foundation the rest of the volume builds on.** The result is food and water governed like a record: receipted, hash-chained, mandate-scoped, origin-bound. That is what makes the deeper guarantees possible — because the good is a governed object with a portable receipt and a bound origin, it can be provisioned locally with no central provisioner (Chapter 3), require its origin (Chapter 4), and be verified by its receipt (Chapter 5). The good is one; its receipt travels; its origin is part of it. **In the acceptance tests, a food good provisions as a receipted object with its quantity, kind, and origin -- so the traceable-good discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_provisions_sustenance_as_receipted_object` proves the receipt's shape and content. For the Ridgeline homestead, this means a harvest is provisioned as `MaterialGood:food:heirloom-wheat:north-field-2026`, a hash-chained object under the homestead's mandate, with a receipt the food carries and an origin bound into its identity. Chapter 3 shows why that registry is the homestead's own — and why there is no central provisioner in the loop.

title: S9 03 Food Water
chapter_title: No Central Provisioner -- Each Node Provisions Its Own
text: You will see the first discipline that makes provisioned sustenance sovereign -- provision_sustenance writes into the node's OWN local registry, never a central chain -- so no node depends on a provisioner it does not control, and its food and water are held, not merely labeled.

title: S9 03 Food Water
chapter_title: No Central Provisioner -- Each Node Provisions Its Own
text: **Sovereignly provisioned sustenance is held by the node itself -- provision_sustenance writes into the node's own registry, so there is no central provisioner any node depends on.** The danger with food and water is the chain: a single distributor every node must go through to record or confirm a good. This chapter refuses it. `provision_sustenance` takes the node's own registry and writes there — inheriting the Material Primitive's no-central-provisioner discipline, now applied to sustenance. Each node provisions into the registry it holds. **The registry is the node's own -- provision_sustenance takes it as a parameter and writes there, so a good is recorded where the node holds it, not in a chain's database across a network.** The locality is explicit. `provision_sustenance` knows about no central store; it writes to the registry the caller passes, the node's own. A harvest is recorded where it was grown. There is no moment where the node must reach a distributor to make a provision real. **Two nodes provision independently into their own registries -- each good lives only in the node that produced it, with no shared registry either depends on.** The primitive scales by not sharing. `test_no_central_provisioner_two_local_registries` proves it: Ridgeline provisions a grain harvest into its registry and Cedar provisions spring water into its own; each good lives in exactly one node's registry, and neither node's provision touches the other's store. Two sovereign nodes provisioning sustenance are two independent holders, not two accounts on one chain. **A receipt from one node still verifies at another -- because verify_sustenance checks the receipt itself, a good provisioned at one node is confirmable at any node, with no shared chain.** Locality of holding does not mean isolation of proof. Although each good lives only in its own node's registry, its receipt is portable: `test_no_central_provisioner_two_local_registries` proves one node's good verifies from its receipt alone at another. `verify_sustenance` needs no registry at all. So sustenance is held locally and proofs travel freely — with no central chain that all provisioning depends on. **No central provisioner is what keeps provisioning sovereign -- there is no single system whose outage, capture, or mislabeling breaks every node's ability to provision or confirm its food and water.** A central chain is a single point of failure and control. If every provision had to be recorded in one system, that system's outage would halt provisioning everywhere, its compromise would corrupt every node's provenance, and its operator would hold power over all of them. By writing to each node's own registry, `provision_sustenance` removes that point. There is nothing to capture that would break the whole. **Local provisioning mirrors the sovereignty of local records, goods, and power -- a node holds its sustenance as it holds its records, on its own storage, under its own mandate, answerable to no central authority.** The primitive is consistent with the whole stack. A sovereign node keeps its records, goods, and energy on its own storage under its own mandate; now it keeps its food and water the same way. There is no more a central sustenance authority than there is a central records authority. Ridgeline's harvest is Ridgeline's — provisioned and governed locally. **Sustenance held locally with a portable receipt is both sovereign and shareable -- the node depends on no chain, and any receiver can still verify, which the rest of the volume builds on.** The result is provisioning that is neither centralized nor siloed. A good is held by exactly one node, dependent on no external chain, and yet its receipt lets any receiver confirm it and its origin. Because provisioning is local and the receipt is portable, the origin can be required (Chapter 4) and the weakest receiver can verify it (Chapter 5). Held locally; provable anywhere. **In the acceptance tests, two nodes provision into their own registries and each verifies the other's good by receipt -- so the no-central-provisioner discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_no_central_provisioner_two_local_registries` proves the independent local registries and the cross-node verification by receipt. For Ridgeline and its neighbor Cedar, this means each homestead provisions its own sustenance on its own storage, and either can confirm the other's good from the receipt that travels with it — no shared chain. Chapter 4 makes the origin non-optional.

title: S9 03 Food Water
chapter_title: Traceable Origin -- Regenerative Provenance, Never Absent
text: You will see the discipline that makes sustenance trustworthy -- a food or water good must name a traceable origin, of a real kind, in a real quantity, and any change to the origin flips verification to tampered -- so a good's provenance is never absent, faked, or swapped.

title: S9 03 Food Water
chapter_title: Traceable Origin -- Regenerative Provenance, Never Absent
text: **A traceable good names its origin -- provision_sustenance refuses a food or water good with no origin, so provenance is required, not optional.** A record of sustenance is only as trustworthy as its origin. This chapter builds the guard that fits food and water. `provision_sustenance` refuses a good with no traceable origin — regenerative provenance is not optional — so a harvest or a tank cannot be provisioned as coming from nowhere. The origin enters the receipt, or the provision does not happen. **An absent origin is refused -- provision_sustenance fails closed on a good with no provenance, so sustenance cannot be provisioned as coming from nowhere.** The guard is fail-closed. `test_origin_required` proves it: a good with an empty origin raises before anything is recorded. A food or water good has a source by physical fact, and the primitive enforces that fact — a good with no origin is not provisioned, so no untraceable sustenance ever enters a receipt. The good names where it came from, or it is not provisioned. **The kind must be food or water, and the quantity must be real -- so a sustenance good is well-formed, of a known kind, in a non-negative amount.** Honesty is also about form. `test_kind_must_be_food_or_water` proves a good of an unknown kind is refused, and `test_negative_quantity_refused` proves a negative quantity is refused. A sustenance good is of a known kind and a real amount — not an ambiguous category or an impossible quantity. What was provisioned is well-formed by construction. **A swapped origin flips verification to tampered -- because the origin is bound into the good's identity and the hash-chained receipt, a changed source does not re-derive.** The strongest guarantee is that provenance cannot be silently swapped. `test_verify_sustenance_detects_a_tampered_origin` proves it: a receipt checked against a different origin than the one provisioned fails to verify. Because the origin is part of the good's identity and the hash-chained receipt, any change to it — a substitution, a mislabel — is detectable, and `verify_sustenance` flips to tampered. A good's source cannot be quietly changed to claim a provenance it does not have; the receipt either re-derives with the real origin or fails. **A required, verifiable origin matters because sustenance is a trust of safety -- a mislabeled source is not a harmless error but a false claim about what a person is eating or drinking, which is why the guard is strict.** It matters that this lands on food and water. Origin is not decoration; it is a claim of safety, of provenance, of what a person is putting into their body. A mislabeled source is a false claim about that. Requiring origin and catching its substitution is not fussiness — it is what keeps a sustenance record from becoming a way to disguise where food and water came from. The strictness is proportionate to the stake. **The origin guard composes the primitive's integrity -- provision_sustenance adds the required-origin check, and the hash-chained tamper-evidence is the Material Primitive's, so provenance is layered, not re-implemented.** The primitive rolls no new integrity. `provision_sustenance` adds exactly the domain guards — origin required, kind and quantity well-formed — and inherits the tamper-evidence from the Material Primitive's hash-chained receipt. So an honest origin is guarded twice: at entry (required, bound into identity) and forever after (tamper-evident), the second borrowed from the sealed floor. The sustenance volume contributes the provenance requirement; the cryptographic honesty is the primitive's, composed. **A source that cannot be absent or swapped is a good a node can stand behind -- which the receiver, and the safety it rests on, can rely on.** The result is a provenance trustworthy at both ends: it could not have been absent when recorded, and it cannot have been swapped since. A receiver checking a good's receipt reads the origin it actually came from. That is what makes sustenance safe to hand on: the source is required at entry and immutable after. Chapter 5 shows how any receiver — even the weakest — verifies all of this from the receipt alone. **In the acceptance tests, an absent origin, an unknown kind, and a negative quantity are refused, and a swapped origin fails verification -- so the traceable-origin discipline is executable and proven, not asserted.** `test_origin_required`, `test_kind_must_be_food_or_water`, `test_negative_quantity_refused`, and `test_verify_sustenance_detects_a_tampered_origin` prove the cases.
